best_for: Design teams on Windows or macOS who want Figma in its own window, using the fonts already on the computer.
description:
Figma is a design tool from Figma, Inc. for laying out apps, websites and other screens, and for turning those layouts into prototypes. The same company also makes FigJam for whiteboards and Figma Slides for presentations.

Several people can work in one file at the same time, leave comments on the canvas and talk through cursor chat without leaving the design. You can store colors, styles and components in a shared library so every screen uses the same parts. Vector tools with brushes and stroke settings cover drawing. Figma also has a built-in AI agent you can ask for new design directions or bulk edits to text and images, right on the canvas. Figma Motion adds timeline animation to your designs.

points.title: Same editor as the browser
points.text: Figma's help says the desktop app has the same features as the web version. The reason to install it is tabs, separate windows and access to the fonts on your computer.

points.title: An account is required
points.text: You sign in with email and password, Google single sign-on or SAML.

points.title: Windows and macOS only
points.text: Official desktop apps exist for macOS 13 or later (Intel and Apple Silicon) and 64-bit Windows 10 or later (x64 and Arm). We found no Linux desktop app, so Linux users work in the browser.

points.title: Fonts come from your computer
points.text: The app uses fonts installed on the device. A small background helper called FigmaAgent is the font installer; the desktop app does not need it.

points.title: Free plan limits
points.text: The free Starter plan lists unlimited drafts and 150 AI credits a day, up to 500 a month. Anyone can be invited to view, comment, inspect or export for free.

points.title: Paid seats
points.text: Professional lists a Full seat at USD 16 a month, a Dev seat at USD 12 (adds Dev Mode and 500 AI credits) and a Collab seat at USD 3. Billing terms were not clear on the page.

points.title: Windows has two installers
points.text: Windows gets a per-user .exe and a machine-wide MSI, which helps IT teams that deploy for all users.
